title: Fake QR Code at Parking? Spot THIS Before You Pay! #Shorts
description:
That parking-meter QR code may not be the original. The FTC warned in September 2026 that scammers can cover legitimate codes with fake stickers and redirect people to imitation payment pages. This original animated Short demonstrates three habits: check for stickers or tampering, inspect the full destination URL before opening it, and use the parking operator's verified app or website when uncertain. The QR image and payment screen shown are FICTIONAL and nonfunctional; no real payment was made or personal data collected. Original synthesized ambient music and sound effects; synthetic Kokoro narration.

FTC September 2026: https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2026/09/see-qr-code-parked-somewhere-dont-scan-ityet

captions.text: Before you scan a parking-meter QR code, here's a three-second warning.
In September twenty twenty-six, the Federal Trade Commission warned that scammers can cover real parking codes with fake stickers.
A fake code can send you to a convincing payment page, where entering your card details could expose them.
First, check if a new sticker covers the original code.
Second, preview the full website address and look for altered spelling.
Third, if you're unsure, use the parking company's official app or website instead.
QR codes are useful, but blind trust is risky; pause, check, then pay.
